analysis.investment_thesis: Bajaj Electricals is a stagnant consumer appliances business with 0.6% revenue CAGR over 9 years, negative operating margins (-2.1%), and a 7.1% ROE — priced at a grotesque 120x trailing P/E. This is precisely the kind of mediocre business at a terrible price I have spent my career avoiding.
key_strengths: Bajaj brand carries genuine recognition across India's mass-market consumer segment
Borrowings slashed from INR 1,084 Cr (2020) to INR 215 Cr (2025), showing balance sheet discipline
OCF positive all 5 years with INR 318 Cr FCF in 2025 — the business does generate some cash
key_risks: Valuation is indefensible: 120x P/E and 33x EV/EBITDA for a business growing revenue at 0.6% CAGR over 9 years
Negative operating margin (-2.1%) means the core business isn't earning its keep — profitability rests on other income (INR 76 Cr)
Highly commoditized, intensely competitive market (Havells, Crompton, Orient, Voltas) with no evident pricing power
red_flags: Operating margin is NEGATIVE at -2.1% — a consumer brand with 85 years of history should not be margin-negative
Revenue in 2025 (INR 4,826 Cr) is barely above 2016 levels (INR 4,590 Cr) — a decade of zero real growth
Net profit trend is contracting despite revenue stability; profit swings wildly (loss in 2020, INR 216 Cr in 2023, now INR 133 Cr)
OCF deteriorating sharply: INR 914 Cr in 2022 → INR 347 Cr in 2025 — cash generation quality is declining fast
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bajaj Electricals is a textbook example of a business I have no interest in owning at any elevated price. Revenue has compounded at a mere 0.6% annually over nine years — barely keeping pace with inflation — while the stock commands 120x trailing earnings. The ROE of 7.1% and ROCE of 11.6% tell me this business earns a mediocre return on the capital deployed within it. When a consumer brand with the Bajaj name behind it cannot generate positive operating margins, the moat is clearly shallow. The competitive landscape — Havells, Crompton, Orient, Voltas — has commoditized nearly every product category Bajaj Electricals participates in, from fans to kitchen appliances to LED lighting.

The balance sheet repair (debt down from INR 1,084 Cr to INR 215 Cr) is commendable, and the brand has genuine recall value in Tier 2/3 India. But positive attributes end there. FCF has fallen from INR 871 Cr in 2022 to INR 318 Cr in 2025, operating cash flows are shrinking, and the path to a meaningful re-rating requires a margin turnaround that nothing in the last decade suggests is forthcoming. Even on the optimistic forward P/E of 28.75x, I would need to see durable double-digit earnings growth and ROE above 15% to get excited — neither is remotely visible in this data. At INR 391, the market is pricing in a transformation story with no evidence it exists.
